metaTitle: Best 20 Inch Snow Blowers, Corded and Cordless
metaDescription: Six 20 inch single stage snow blowers compared by intake depth, throw distance, auger type, battery runtime and cord limits, for paved driveways and walks.
expertTake: The WORX WG461 is the best 20 inch snow blower for most paved driveways: a brushless 40V machine that throws up to 35 feet and claims a 15 car driveway per charge in 6 inch snow. The Greenworks 80V is the pick for anyone already on that platform, and the Westinghouse WSnow20 is the best corded value. If your driveway is gravel, or you routinely get more than 10 inches at a time, skip this size class and buy a two stage machine.
introParagraphs: A 20 inch snow blower is almost always a single stage machine: one rubber edged auger scoops snow and flings it straight out the chute in one motion. That makes it light, simple and quick to start, and perfect for paved driveways and walks after moderate storms. The weak points are deep, wet snow and the plow ridge at the end of the drive, and spec sheets rarely explain those limits honestly.

This guide explains how intake depth, auger material and throw distance shape real performance, how battery and corded power compare in cold weather, and why surface type rules out single stage machines for some homes. Quick picks are above, and detailed reviews follow below.

products.name: WORX WG461 40V 20 in Brushless Cordless Snow Blower

specList.label: Runtime claim
specList.value: Up to a 15 car driveway in 6 in snow

products.description:
WORX runs a brushless motor from two 20V 6.0 Ah PowerShare Pro packs in series for 40V, clearing a 20 by 10 inch path and throwing up to 35 feet. Throw distance matters more than most buyers think: a longer throw lets you clear a wide driveway by casting snow off the edge instead of piling it on the next pass. WORX claims a 15 car driveway per charge in 6 inch snow.

Against the STEELITE 40V and ETOOLAB at 25 feet, the WORX throws 10 feet farther, and its 12 Ah of total battery is the most in the cordless group apart from the Greenworks 80V's higher voltage pack. The PowerShare platform also runs WORX mowers and trimmers.

Keep batteries indoors until you go out, since cold lithium cells deliver less power. After use, knock snow out of the chute and auger so it does not freeze solid.
products.bestFor: Paved two car driveways with moderate snowfalls and owners who want no cord.
pros: 35 ft throw clears wide drives without re-piling snow
Two 6.0 Ah packs give a large runtime reserve
Brushless motor holds auger speed in heavier snow
Batteries run other WORX PowerShare tools
cons: 10 in intake depth limits deeper storms to multiple passes
Single stage design is unsuitable for gravel drives

products.name: Greenworks 80V 20 in Brushless Snow Blower, 4 Ah Kit
products.description:
Greenworks uses its 80V platform with a brushless motor, clearing a 20 inch wide, 10 inch deep path. An 80V 4.0 Ah pack stores about the same energy as the WORX's two 20V 6.0 Ah packs, but the higher voltage lets the motor pull less current for the same power, which helps it hold auger speed in dense snow.

The kit has one battery, so you cannot swap a second pack mid job unless you own one. If you already use Greenworks 80V mowers or blowers, this is the natural pick. Against the WORX, throw distance is not stated, so we rank it second.

The fast charger means a quick top up between storms. Clear the chute after use and store the pack indoors.
products.bestFor: Greenworks 80V owners clearing paved driveways and walks.
pros: 80V platform delivers strong, efficient power
Brushless motor is quiet and needs no maintenance
Fast charger refills between storms
Shares batteries with 80V mowers and blowers
cons: Single battery kit limits runtime without a spare

products.name: STEELITE 40V (2 x 20V) 20 in Cordless Snow Blower
products.description:
STEELITE's cordless model runs a brushless motor from two 20V 4.0 Ah packs and claims 850 pounds per minute, with a 12 inch intake depth and a 25 foot throw. At 26 pounds it is easy to lift onto steps or a deck. A deeper 12 inch intake helps in heavier dumps where 10 inch machines need extra passes.

Compared with the WORX, you trade 10 feet of throw and 4 Ah of battery for a lower price and a deeper intake. It is a strong value for paved driveways and walks.

Run it at the start of a storm rather than waiting for full depth, which keeps load and runtime in check. Keep batteries warm before use.
products.bestFor: Budget minded owners of paved drives who want a cordless machine.
pros: 12 in intake handles deeper snow than 10 in rivals
Light 26 lb build lifts easily onto steps
Two batteries included
Claimed 850 lb per minute capacity
cons: 25 ft throw is 10 ft shorter than the WORX

products.name: Westinghouse WSnow20 20 in Corded Snow Blower, Steel Auger
products.description:
The WSnow20 is a corded machine with a 15 amp, 1800 watt motor and a rubber tipped steel auger, clearing 680 pounds per minute through a 20 by 10 inch path. A steel auger with rubber edges is tougher than an all plastic paddle when it hits ice chunks, while the rubber still protects pavement. Westinghouse also sells a WSnow20D version with a plastic auger, which is the cheaper but less durable variant.

Corded power never runs out and does not weaken in cold the way batteries do. Against the STEELITE corded at 860 lb per minute, the Westinghouse claims less but has a better known brand behind it. The cord limits range on long drives.

Use a cold rated outdoor extension cord of adequate gauge, plugged into a GFCI outlet. Clear the chute after use.
products.bestFor: Short paved driveways and walks near an outlet.
pros: Unlimited runtime with no batteries to warm or charge
Rubber tipped steel auger resists ice chunk damage
Dual LED lights for early morning clearing
Recognized brand with simple maintenance
cons: Cord management on long or curved drives
680 lb per minute is lower than the STEELITE corded

products.name: STEELITE 20 in Corded Snow Blower, 15A Brushless
products.description:
This STEELITE pairs a corded 15 amp brushless motor with a 20 by 10 inch intake, claiming 860 pounds per minute and a 30 foot throw. Brushless motors on corded tools are uncommon; they hold speed better under load and have no brushes to wear. It is clearly labeled as corded, not battery.

Its claims beat the Westinghouse's 680 lb per minute and match the STEELITE cordless capacity with no runtime limit. The brand is newer, so long term support is less proven than Westinghouse.

As with any corded blower, use a heavy gauge outdoor cord and keep it behind you. Clear wet snow from the chute before storing.
products.bestFor: Owners near an outlet who want more throw and capacity than basic corded units.
pros: 860 lb per minute claim leads the corded group
30 ft throw beats most single stage rivals
Brushless corded motor with no runtime limit
LED lights for dark mornings
cons: Cord limits reach on long drives
Newer brand with less proven support

products.name: ETOOLAB 40V 20 in Cordless Snow Blower

specList.label: Throw
specList.value: Up to 25 ft away, 20 ft high

products.description:
ETOOLAB's 40V machine uses a 2500 RPM brushless motor, a 12 inch deep intake and a 180 degree chute, throwing up to 25 feet away and 20 feet high. The high arc helps clear over snowbanks along a driveway.

It matches the STEELITE cordless on depth and throw. Battery details are less clear, so we rank it below the STEELITE, which includes two 4.0 Ah packs. It is a reasonable choice for patios, decks and short drives.

Store it with the chute clear and the battery indoors. Check auger paddles each season for wear.
products.bestFor: Decks, patios and short paved drives with occasional deep snow.
pros: 12 in intake depth handles deeper falls
High 20 ft arc clears over banks
Brushless motor
180° chute directs snow away from doors and cars
cons: Battery specifics less clearly stated than rivals
25 ft throw is shorter than the WORX

buyingCriteria.explanation: Single stage blowers clear by letting the auger touch the ground, which is why they clean pavement so well. On gravel, the same auger picks up stones and throws them, damaging the machine and anything nearby. Every machine in this lineup is single stage, so all suit paved surfaces only.

Intake depth is the tallest snow the housing accepts in one pass. The STEELITE cordless and ETOOLAB take 12 inches, while the WORX, Greenworks and Westinghouse take 10. For deeper storms, clear in stages during the snowfall.

A longer throw puts snow past the edge of the drive instead of into your next pass. The WORX throws up to 35 feet, the STEELITE corded 30 and the STEELITE cordless and ETOOLAB 25. On a two car driveway, 30 feet or more saves real time.

Cords never run out and are not weakened by cold, but limit range and need a GFCI outlet. Batteries are free to roam but lose capacity in cold. The WORX's two 6.0 Ah packs provide the largest reserve here.
Steel augers with rubber tips, like on the Westinghouse WSnow20, survive ice chunks better than plastic paddles. The cheaper WSnow20D uses plastic. Rubber edges protect pavement and wear over time.

Pounds per minute claims like the STEELITE's 850 and 860 assume light, fluffy snow at full depth. Wet snow is several times denser and slows any single stage machine. Use the figure for comparison only.

specDecoder.meaning: The width of path cleared per pass. All picks here clear 20 inches.
specDecoder.watchFor: Width counts less than depth and throw for real speed.

specDecoder.meaning: The height of the auger housing opening, which sets maximum depth per pass.
specDecoder.watchFor: Machines can bog well before the stated depth in wet snow.

specDecoder.meaning: How far snow lands from the chute in ideal snow.
specDecoder.watchFor: Measured in dry snow; wet snow throws much shorter.

specDecoder.meaning: Mass of snow moved per minute, a capacity estimate.
specDecoder.watchFor: Rarely standardized; compare only within a brand or treat as approximate.

specDecoder.meaning: One auger both gathers and throws snow, contacting the ground.
specDecoder.watchFor: Not suitable for gravel; two stage machines keep the auger above the surface.

howWeEvaluated.title: Clearing performance
howWeEvaluated.description: We combined intake depth, throw distance and capacity claims. The WORX's 35 ft throw led, while 12 in intakes on the STEELITE cordless and ETOOLAB scored for depth. Unpublished specs lowered rankings.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and runtime
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared battery voltage and capacity and corded motor ratings. The WORX's 12 Ah total and Greenworks 80V led cordless. Corded units scored for unlimited runtime.

howWeEvaluated.title: Durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighted auger material and brand track record. The Westinghouse rubber tipped steel auger scored well. Plastic auger variants were noted as cheaper but weaker.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cold weather usability
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered battery cold performance, LED lights and chute controls. Corded machines scored for cold reliability. Lights helped dark morning use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Platform and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed whether batteries run other tools and how established each brand is. WORX and Greenworks scored highest. Newer brands lost points on support.

cards.label: Cordless
cards.text: Roam anywhere, but cold reduces battery output and runtime is fixed. In this roundup: WORX WG461, Greenworks 80V, STEELITE 40V and ETOOLAB 40V.

cards.label: Corded
cards.text: Never run out and not affected by cold, but tied to an outlet and cord length. In this roundup: Westinghouse WSnow20 and STEELITE Corded 20 in.

howToChoose.note: Choose corded for short drives near an outlet; choose cordless for longer or more complex layouts.

rows: Runs a full drive per charge

howToChoose.subheading: For End of Driveway Plow Ridges Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Plow ridges are dense, compacted snow that challenges every single stage machine. A steel auger, a strong motor and taking small bites help.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse WSnow20's rubber tipped steel auger and the WORX WG461's brushless motor handle ridges best, cutting a few inches at a time.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You have a longer drive or already own WORX or Greenworks batteries. The WORX WG461 or Greenworks 80V pays back in throw and runtime.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You clear a short walk or drive near an outlet. The Westinghouse WSnow20 or STEELITE corded does the job for less.

maintenance.task: Clear snow from chute and auger
maintenance.why: Leftover snow refreezes and locks the auger. Starting against a frozen auger can damage belts or motors.
Worn rubber leaves snow behind and lets metal hit pavement. Replace them when thin.
The scraper bar wears against pavement. A worn bar reduces clearing quality.
Cold lithium cells deliver less power and charge poorly. Warm packs give full runtime.
Cold cracks cord insulation. A damaged cord is a shock hazard.

faq.q: Can I use a 20 inch snow blower on gravel?
faq.a: Not safely; single stage augers touch the ground and throw stones. Use a two stage machine on gravel.

faq.q: How deep a snowfall can these handle?
faq.a: Up to their intake depth, 10 or 12 inches, in light snow. For deeper or wet snow, clear in stages during the storm.

faq.q: Do batteries work well in freezing weather?
faq.a: They work but deliver less. Keep packs indoors until use and bring spares for big drives.

faq.q: What cord do I need for a corded blower?
faq.a: An outdoor cord rated for cold, of adequate gauge for the length, plugged into a GFCI outlet. Thicker gauge reduces voltage drop.

faq.q: Is a longer throw distance really important?
faq.a: Yes on wider drives, because it puts snow past the edge instead of in your next pass. It matters less on narrow walks.

faq.q: Why does my snow blower clog?
faq.a: Wet snow sticks inside the chute. Spraying the chute with a non stick coating before use and clearing early in the storm reduces clogs.
